This collapse in revenue generation is mirrored by a consistent erosion of shareholder value, with compounded share price growth remaining negative across all measured timeframes, including a -29% decline over the past year [E17, E18, E19, E20]. Furthermore, the bear’s reliance on the 52-week range [E4] ignores that the company is currently flagged for strong sales growth [E48, E49] and profit growth exceeding 20% YoY [E51]. By fixating on past decay rather than the recent, verified surge in profitability, the bear overlooks the evidence that the company is beginning to outperform expectations [E41].

The bull’s reliance on recent profit growth [E16, E51] ignores the terminal reality of a business that has seen its compounded sales growth collapse to -100% over the trailing twelve months [E15]. However, this statistical anomaly occurs against a backdrop of a decade-long -60% compounded sales decline [E12] and consistent share price erosion [E17, E18, E19, E20].
